stories.title: Recall effort fails against officials who greenlit massive tech facility
stories.dek: A Michigan clerk has rejected petitions aimed at recalling local officials who approved rezoning for a massive data center project. Residents opposed to the development now face an uphill battle to force a new vote. The decision keeps the 500-acre project on track in a community already divided over power use and tax breaks.
stories.source_title: Michigan clerk rejects recall petitions in fight over 500-acre data center rezoning - Yahoo

stories.title: Saline data center project pushes ahead despite new rules and pushback
stories.dek: The Saline Township data center proposal is advancing even as local officials tighten zoning rules under political pressure. The project could bring thousands of construction jobs but also heavy power and water demands. Residents 30 miles away will feel the impact through higher utility rates and tax shifts.
stories.source_title: Weekly Data Center Watch: Saline Project Advances Amid New Rules and Political Pressure - The Sun Times News

stories.title: DTE seeks two new gas plants to feed data center power hunger
stories.dek: DTE Energy plans to ask state regulators for permission to build two natural gas plants as data centers drive up electricity demand across southeast Michigan. The move comes as older coal units retire and could push up customer bills if the plants are approved. Residents from Detroit to Ann Arbor will feel the impact through higher rates and more fossil fuel generation.
stories.source_title: DTE will seek approval for 2 natural gas plants as coal phases out, data centers go online - Planet Detroit

stories.title: Two more Metro Detroit towns rewrite rules to curb data centers
stories.dek: Local officials in two additional suburbs are changing zoning codes after residents raised alarms over noise, water use and power strain. The changes could block or slow large projects that developers have eyed in the region. Homeowners 30 miles away may see ripple effects on property values and utility costs.
stories.source_title: Two more Metro Detroit communities move to amend data center zoning - The Detroit News

stories.title: Wixom sued by data center firm after city blocks project
stories.dek: A developer is taking Wixom to court, claiming the city’s zoning decisions unfairly killed its data center plans. The lawsuit could force taxpayers to cover legal costs and delay other local projects. Oakland County residents will watch to see if the fight chills future investment or protects neighborhoods from heavy industrial loads.
stories.source_title: Data center developer sues Wixom, impacts city decisions - The Detroit News

stories.title: Solon Township extends data center freeze another six months
stories.dek: Solon Township leaders recommended keeping the existing moratorium in place through early next year. The extension blocks new proposals while the township updates zoning rules to address resident concerns about noise, traffic and utility costs. West Michigan communities nearby are watching the decision closely.
stories.source_title: Solon Twp. board recommends extending data center moratorium for another six months - WZZM13.com

stories.title: West Michigan town extends data center ban another 6 months
stories.dek: A West Michigan community has pushed its moratorium on new data centers out to at least early 2027. Residents gain more time to examine power demand, noise, and water use before any large projects can move forward. The extension keeps local officials from approving facilities that could strain the grid and raise utility bills for nearby homes.
stories.source_title: West Michigan town adds 6 more months on data center moratorium - NewsBreak: Local News & Alerts

stories.title: Homeowners to get decibel readings that could halt server farm near residences
stories.dek: Officials in Gaines Township will measure sound levels at a proposed data center location to see how much residents would hear. The study could block or reshape the project if cooling fans and generators exceed local limits. Homeowners within a few miles now have concrete data to judge whether the facility will disturb daily life.
stories.source_title: Gaines Township to research noise at proposed data center site - Yahoo

stories.title: Michigan supervisors back bills to curb data center power costs
stories.dek: Township leaders across northern Michigan endorsed new state rules that would force data centers to pay more toward grid upgrades. Residents could see lower electric bills if the bills pass, but only if local governments keep leverage over big projects. The move signals growing pushback against unlimited data center growth in the state.
stories.source_title: Supervisors back state bills regulating data centers - North County Pipeline

stories.title: Garfield Twp halts data centers for a year to study rules
stories.dek: Garfield Township supervisors voted to pause all new data-center proposals while they research limits on power use, water draw and noise. The move gives residents time to weigh how large server farms would affect local taxes, roads and the power grid in Grand Traverse County. Without the pause, developers could file applications before any new restrictions take effect.
stories.source_title: Garfield Township enacts data center moratorium to buy time for research on restrictions - 9and10News.com

stories.title: Lowell Twp still hammering out rules for big data centers
stories.dek: Lowell Township continues work on an ordinance to govern data center siting after months of debate. The rules will decide where these facilities can locate and what limits apply to power and noise. Kent County residents should pay attention because the outcome will shape future development and local tax impacts.
stories.source_title: ‘Long way to go’: Work continues on data center ordinance in Lowell Township - AOL.ca

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
